items.title: Sweeter than honey
items.description: WE live in a world where tech giants like the frankly disturbing Peter Thiel rant about the antichrist and the excessively wealthy and extremely unlovable Elon Musk tries to foment racial discord via his own social media platform and names his children things like Tau Techno Mechanicus. What I’m saying is that things are weird, and getting weirder with every passing moment and so, it’s a relief to learn that (former) Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is at least a human being who succumbed not to the desire to turn himself into a cyborg but instead to the charms of a lady who may or may not be a Chinese spy out to milk him for critical tech-related information; the jury is still out on that but the verdict will come too late for Mr Huang. Nevertheless, if true, he fell for what is arguably one of the — if not the — oldest tricks in the book: the honeytrap. The first recorded mention of this classic gambit is in the Biblical story of Samson and Delilah. Samson, as the story goes, was a superhero of the ancient world whose great strength was the bane of his enemies. Naturally wanting to somehow weaken him by learning the source of his strength and negating it, his opponents found the beautiful and seductive Delilah who inveigled her way into his confidence and, having learned that the source of his strength was his long hair, proceeded to shave his head while he slept and thus allowed his enemies to capture him. But the real heyday of the honeytraps was during the world wars and then the Cold War. Here, I must caution those who may be thinking that falling for such a ploy is exclusively a male weakness. It’s not: Roald Dahl, the famous British author, apparently also served as a honeytrap whose mission was to win the hearts and minds of influential female writers, politicians and socialites in the United States so as to build a consensus in favour of the Allied war efforts. He was perfect for the job: a ‘skilled flirt’, standing at six foot six inches in his pilot’s uniform, oozing old-world charm and chock-full of wit, Dahl blazed a path through American high society in the early forties, famously seducing oil heiress Millicent Rogers and having an affair with Congresswoman Clare Booth Luce in an attempt to soften her views towards the British Empire. Success has its own drawbacks, and Dahl reportedly found the liaisons with the lawmaker so physically exhausting that he begged to be relieved of this duty only to be told to close his eyes and think of England. After all, much needs to be sacrificed for the greater national interest. The heyday of honeytraps was during the world wars & the Cold War. Dahl isn’t the only ‘Romeo spy’ on record as the East German Stasi — which ran one of the most pervasive intelligence networks to ever exist — operated an entire department of handsome and charismatic male spies to target lonely and vulnerable ‘Juliets’ who worked as assistants and secretaries in West German ministries, Nato offices, Western embassies and so on. It worked like a charm, providing the Eastern Bloc a steady stream of classified information. Honeytraps also need to be flexible enough to cater to any predilection, as the KGB demonstrated in the 1950s with British civil servant John Vassal, who was posted in the British embassy in Moscow. Quickly realising that Vassal was a repressed homosexual in an age where this practice was illegal in both Britain and the Soviet Union, they trapped him by using a Polish man to entice him into imbibing large amounts of alcohol at an ‘underground’ party for homosexuals in which he was photographed in compromising positions with a series of young men who had been trained precisely for this purpose. In fact, the entire party had been arranged by the KGB. With their hooks deep in him, the Soviets milked him for information that proved to be of the highest value to the Soviet defence chiefs in their successful drive to expand and modernise the Red Navy. The oddest honeytrap story of all time has to be the tale of French diplomat Bernard Boursicort, which has been immortalised in the play M. Butterfly, which was later turned into a film starring Jeremy Irons. Stationed in Beijing in the 60s, Boursicort began a 20-year affair with Chinese opera singer Shi Pei Pu who claimed to be a woman forced to dress like a man so that she could satisfy her father’s wish to have a son. In due course, while pressuring Boursicort into passing on several hundred secret documents and plying him with misinformation, she also produced a child that she claimed was the fruit of their liaisons. That was of course impossible because when they were finally arrested in 1983 it turned out that Pei had been a man all along. How did he then fool Boursicort for so long, given the intimate nature of their relationship? Well, you’ll just have to look that up yourself. The writer is a journalist. X: @zarrarkhuhro Published in Dawn, November 16th, 2026

items.title: Sabalenka apologises and says viral comment ‘not directed at Svitolina’
items.description: Aryna Sabalenka has apologised and denied claims that she insulted opponent Elina Svitolina after a viral clip showed her swearing during her WTA Finals defeat by the Ukrainian. A video of world number two Sabalenka angrily gesturing and swearing in Russian during her 6-3 3-6 6-1 defeat by Ukraine’s Svitolina was posted on social media on Saturday. Some commentators interpreted Belarusian Sabalenka’s comments as an insult towards Svitolina or Ukrainians in general. Sabalenka later wrote on social media that “my comment was not directed at Elina” but she lost her temper because of the behaviour of some fans. “I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment,” the 28-year-old wrote. “That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone offended.” Sabalenka said Svitolina had played a great match, adding that she wished her “all the best for the rest of the tournament”. I hope matches between us are respected – Svitolina Ukrainian players have a long-standing policy of not shaking hands with Russian or Belarusian players because of the ongoing invasion of their country. They also do not take pre-match photographs with each other. But Svitolina, who says she has seen viral clips of Sabalenka’s outburst on social media, hopes the matches between the two will be “respected”. In response to Sabalenka’s statement, Svitolina said on Saturday: “As we see there’s many, many Ukrainians, many, many flags and of course they want me to win this particular match. “We’ve played many times with Aryna. She has her fans. I have my fans. “I just hope the matches between us [are] respected. Sometimes in some matches that we’ve played also there have been not great comments towards me in regards of the war. “It is like this in the social media, sometimes the things are turned around a little bit.” Svitolina will face Mirra Andreeva in the WTA Finals showpiece after thrashing Linda Noskova in the semi-finals. The Ukrainian was composed and aggressive in a 6-2 6-1 victory over Wimbledon champion Noskova in just 64 minutes.

items.title: Burkina Faso : Le pasteur Siaka Traoré désavoue les malédictions de Makosso contre le président du Faso
items.description: Le pasteur burkinabè Siaka Traoré est monté au créneau après les propos de malédiction attribués à Makosso à l'endroit du président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Dans une déclaration publique, l'homme de Dieu appelle à distinguer les désaccords avec les autorités des paroles de malédiction. Les propos attribués à Makosso contre le président burkinabè, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, suscitent des réactions dans les milieux religieux. Au Burkina Faso, le pasteur Siaka Traoré a décidé de prendre position en condamnant les paroles de malédiction visant le chef de l'État. Dans sa déclaration, le responsable religieux rappelle qu'il est possible d'être en désaccord avec une autorité sans pour autant lui souhaiter du mal. « On peut avoir des divergences avec une autorité sans pour autant lui souhaiter le mal ! », a-t-il fait valoir. S'adressant directement à Makosso, le pasteur a également déclaré : « Makosso, je révoque, au nom de Jésus-Christ, toute parole de malédiction prononcée contre le Président du Burkina Faso. » Des références bibliques pour justifier sa position Pour soutenir son intervention, Siaka Traoré s'appuie notamment sur Romains 12:14, un passage biblique qui recommande de bénir plutôt que de maudire. Il évoque également Romains 13:1-2 et 1 Timothée 2:1-2, des textes qui abordent respectivement le rapport des croyants aux autorités et la nécessité de prier pour les dirigeants. Le pasteur ne présente pas pour autant le respect des autorités comme une obligation d'approuver toutes leurs décisions. Il insiste plutôt sur la distinction entre la critique d'un dirigeant et le fait de lui souhaiter du mal. Un appel à la paix pour le Burkina Faso En conclusion de son intervention, Siaka Traoré a formulé une prière pour le pays : « Que Dieu juge avec justice et que sa bénédiction repose sur le Burkina Faso ! » Cette prise de position remet en débat la responsabilité des responsables religieux dans l'espace public, notamment lorsqu'ils s'expriment sur des personnalités politiques et les autorités nationales. À travers son message, le pasteur Siaka Traoré invite à privilégier les paroles de paix, de prière et de bénédiction, même dans les situations de désaccord. items.title: Burkina : le ministre de la Sécurité appelle à faire des routes des espaces de vie, de sécurité et de respect mutuel
items.description: Le ministre de la Sécurité, Mahamadou Sana, a appelé dimanche à une mobilisation collective pour faire des routes burkinabè des espaces de vie, de sécurité, de respect mutuel et de solidarité, à l’occasion de la 18ᵉ Journée nationale de sensibilisation à la sécurité routière. Dans son message publié à l’occasion de cette journée, couplée à la Journée mondiale du souvenir des victimes des accidents de la route, le ministre de la Sécurité a insisté sur la nécessité de promouvoir des comportements responsables chez tous les usagers de la route. Placée sous le thème « Zéro tolérance pour l’incivisme routier », cette 18ᵉ édition met l’accent sur la responsabilité individuelle et collective dans la prévention des accidents de circulation. Mahamadou Sana a invité les conducteurs, motocyclistes, cyclistes, piétons, élèves et étudiants à faire preuve de prudence, de courtoisie et de civisme en toutes circonstances, tout en respectant les règles de circulation pour préserver les vies humaines. Il a également rappelé que les comportements inciviques sur la route mettent en danger non seulement leurs auteurs, mais aussi les autres usagers. Le premier responsable de la Sécurité a, par ailleurs, réaffirmé la détermination du gouvernement à renforcer la sensibilisation, la prévention, les contrôles et l’application rigoureuse des textes en vigueur. Il a particulièrement exhorté les acteurs du transport routier à veiller au bon état technique de leurs véhicules, au respect des limitations de vitesse, des normes de chargement et du nombre de passagers autorisé, ainsi qu’aux temps de repos indispensables à une conduite sûre. Mahamadou Sana a enfin appelé les parents, les éducateurs, les responsables communautaires et les organisations de la société civile à faire de l’éducation à la sécurité routière une priorité permanente. « Un comportement responsable peut sauver des vies », a-t-il rappelé, soulignant que chacun, à son niveau, a un rôle à jouer dans la promotion de la sécurité routière. items.title: Burkina Faso : Un 6e convoi est arrivé portant à plus de 52 000 personnes rapatriées de Guinée
items.description: Le sixième convoi de rapatriement, arrivé le vendredi 13 novembre 2026, a permis d'accueillir 6 919 personnes. Depuis le début des opérations, 52 325 personnes ont été rapatriées, dont 51 125 hommes et 1 200 femmes. Les opérations de rapatriement des Burkinabè affectés par les événements survenus en Guinée se poursuivent. Dans un communiqué publié le 13 novembre 2026, le Conseil national de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CONASUR) annonce que le nombre total de personnes rapatriées s'élève désormais à 52 325. Le sixième convoi, arrivé à cette date, a permis d'accueillir, d'enregistrer et de prendre en charge 6 919 personnes. Selon les statistiques communiquées par le ministère de la Famille et de la Solidarité, les personnes rapatriées comprennent 51 125 hommes et 1 200 femmes. Parmi les personnes recensées figurent également 11 328 enfants ainsi que 1 370 ressortissants d'autres nationalités. Plus de 10 000 personnes convoyées vers leurs localités d'origine Au-delà de l'accueil des personnes rapatriées, des dispositions ont été prises pour faciliter leur retour dans leurs localités d'origine. Grâce à la mobilisation citoyenne dans les différentes régions administratives, les Conseils régionaux de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CORESUR) ont assuré le convoyage de 10 032 personnes depuis Bobo-Dioulasso vers leurs localités respectives. Ces déplacements s'ajoutent aux initiatives individuelles de retour. Le CONASUR appelle à maintenir la solidarité Dans son communiqué, la ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité, Lieutenant-colonel Passowendé Pélagie Kaboré, présidente du CONASUR, réaffirme l'engagement du gouvernement à poursuivre les opérations de rapatriement. Elle exprime également sa reconnaissance à l'ensemble des acteurs ayant contribué à leur déroulement et appelle les populations à maintenir leur élan de solidarité. Le CONASUR invite enfin les citoyens à faire preuve de responsabilité dans le partage des informations relatives à ces opérations, en privilégiant les sources et les canaux officiels. items.title: Zverev ‘felt a lot of joy’ in first win as world number one
items.description: Alexander Zverev said he felt “a lot of joy” after sweeping aside Rafael Jodar to claim his first victory as world number one in the opening match of the ATP Finals. Germany’s Zverev produced a serving masterclass to beat the fast-rising Spaniard 6-4 6-4. The French and US Open champion dropped only 10 points on serve, landing an astonishing 84% of first serves and hitting 10 aces. The only time Zverev looked troubled was when he went two break points down as he served for the opening set – before saving them with back-to-back aces. Zverev lost his first match as world number one at the Paris Masters in November and said afterwards he was “annoyed” at the reaction to his rise to the top of the rankings. However, he said he felt “quite light” in Turin as he bids to win the season-ending title for a third time. “I felt a lot of joy being out there. In Paris I felt heavy,” the 29-year-old said. “I couldn’t focus on tennis in Paris. I was quite exhausted. So much going on. “I definitely enjoyed the tennis today. I felt light, and I felt like I had control over my body.” Zverev has taken full advantage of a year in which Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner have struggled with injuries, winning two majors and reaching the Wimbledon final. He underlined his status as the world’s best player by walking out on court in Turin in a custom black leather jacket with a number one printed on the back and carrying a gold racquet bag. His performance matched his status, as he put constant pressure on the Jodar serve and dominated with his own first strike. The 20-year-old Jodar is one of the brightest talents in the men’s game, having started the year outside the world’s top 150. Now ranked 11th, he fought hard to stay in touch with Zverev, but could find no way through his serve. Zverev broke him early in the first set with a fine backhand down the line and went up a quick break in the second. He had three further chances for a double-break lead but Jodar saved them, before Zverev served out victory. Ben Shelton, who lost to Zverev in the US Open final, beat France’s Arthur Fils 6-2 3-6 6-3 in the second group game. It is the first time world number four Shelton has won a match at the season-ending event, having lost all three group games last year. Watched on by new coach Juan Carlos Ferrero, Shelton fired down 12 aces and saved three of the four break points he faced to outlast seventh-ranked Fils. In the doubles, Britain’s Henry Patten and Finnish partner Harri Heliovaara began their campaign with a 6-3 5-7 10-4 win over Brazilian pair Rafael Matos and Orlando Luz. Wimbledon champions Patten and Heliovaara are the defending champions in Turin.

items.title: The IWT dilemma
items.description: THE Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) of 1960 has long been heralded as one of the most durable water-sharing agreements in history. Despite multiple wars and decades of profound political animosity between India and Pakistan, the IWT managed to survive, providing a fragile framework for regulating the shared waters of the Indus River system. However, the delicate equilibrium of this treaty has been shattered. The move by India to place the IWT in abeyance is not merely a diplomatic protest; it represents a fundamental strategic pivot. In an era increasingly defined by climate change and existential resource competition, the suspension of the IWT signals a shift toward a new, perilous world order where water security dictates state survival, and historical norms are rapidly eclipsed by the “law of the jungle.” To understand the severity of the hydro-political reality of scarcity, one must look beyond the immediate geopolitical friction and consider the changing hydrology and demography of the region. Climate change is rapidly altering the cryosphere of the Himalayas, which feeds the Indus basin. Glacial retreat, erratic monsoon patterns, and severe, prolonged droughts are making water availability increasingly unpredictable. The World Resources Institute (WRI) provides a stark warning in its Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas, mapping a future where water becomes the most prized — and contentious — resource on the planet. According to WRI projections, vast swathes of the globe, including South Asia, face escalating levels of baseline water stress. By mid-century, trillions of dollars in GDP will be exposed to high water risk as demand drastically outstrips renewable supply . In such a landscape, water is no longer just an environmental issue; it is a fundamental driver of national security. As resources diminish, states are becoming increasingly inward-looking. The international order, which once placed a premium on cooperation, is giving way to a more ruthless framework where states prioritise their own existential needs above collective agreements. In this light, placing the IWT in abeyance is not a temporary diplomatic manoeuvre; it is a strategic preparation of the ground for an eventual unilateral withdrawal. As water scarcity increases, the temptation for an upper-riparian state to leverage control over water flows to secure its own agricultural and energy requirements becomes overwhelming, effectively treating the resource as sovereign property rather than a shared heritage. For Pakistan, the stakes are high because the Indus basin underpins agricultural production, rural livelihoods and food security. The intensification of India’s construction of storage dams along the Chenab River, despite the legal challenges and protests from Pakistan, is part of the strategic calculus and entirely consistent with this new paradigm. These projects allow for greater control, storage, and diversion of water. For Pakistan, an agrarian economy whose very existence relies on the Indus system, this is not a developmental disagreement — it is an existential threat. The Chenab-Beas link tunnel and the Salal sediment bypass illustrate the dilemma. Such projects may be presented as engineering responses to energy needs and sedimentation, yet transferring water between basins or modifying sediment-control infrastructure on a shared river raises both questions and concerns. The legal status and technical details of each project must be assessed individually for cumulative impact and downstream confidence. In August 2026 the Court of Arbitration rejected India’s unilateral abeyance of the treaty and reaffirmed that it remains in force. The court also ordered interim measures restricting specified construction at the Ratle hydroelectric project till 90 days after the Neutral Expert’s final decision expected in July 2027. India’s rejection of the court’s authority leaves a gap between legal pronouncement and practical compliance. The coming decision on pondage, spillways, low-level outlets and sediment flushing will matter, but the deeper question is whether both will accept a credible process for resolving disagreements. If the Neutral Expert and Court of Arbitration reach conflicting conclusions, and one or both governments dismiss the outcome, the treaty risks becoming an instrument that exists formally but no longer commands confidence. An institutional collapse would have consequences extending far beyond the immediate available water. It could erode hydrological data sharing, weaken flood warning cooperation, discourage investment in regional water management and intensify competition over reservoirs and infrastructure. A breakdown could also encourage unilateralism in transboundary river governance endangering peace at a time of growing geopolitical tensions and environmental fragility. The central danger remains the growing uncertainty in a system already under intense human pressure. For Pakistan, the stakes are high because the Indus basin underpins agricultural production, rural livelihoods and food security. For India, the consequences would include a more volatile neighbourhood, heightened diplomatic costs and a precedent that could complicate its own relations with other upstream countries. Neither country can insulate itself from the climatic and economic consequences of a destabilised basin. The gravity of the situation is exacerbated by the nuclear capabilities of both nations. The failure of the current global negotiations in limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius is also ensuring that hydrological instability will only worsen and add to the fear of scarcity. The international community must act before the legal impasse becomes a humanitarian and security crisis. Political wisdom and environmental diplomacy can also play a major role in averting a potential catastrophe. A nuclear-armed upstream power and a highly water-dependent nuclear-armed lower-riparian state cannot afford to let a river become an instrument of existential threat. If water insecurity contributes to political instability, military escalation or a wider regional confrontation, the consequences will not remain confined to South Asia. The writer is a climate policy analyst. aisha@csccc.org.pk Published in Dawn, November 16th, 2026

items.title: Belgium come back to beat Italy to quarters spot
items.description: Belgium qualified for the Nations League quarter-finals at the expense of Italy after coming from behind to beat the Azzurri. Pio Esposito gave Italy the lead with his 10th goal in 15 caps from Brentford defender Michael Kayode’s cross. But Brighton’s Maxim de Cuyper slammed in a Belgian equaliser from six yards out in Brussels. Nathan Ngoy then put the hosts ahead with his first international goal after Brandon Mechele’s header was blocked. Jeremy Doku beat several defenders before slotting the ball past Manchester City team-mate Gianluigi Donnarumma to give them a 3-1 lead. Diego Moreira added a fourth from Kevin de Bruyne’s ball. Italy won a late penalty but Manchester United keeper Senne Lammens saved Esposito’s spot-kick. Mark van Bommel’s Belgium finish second in Group A1, behind France – who beat Turkey 2-1 . Roberto Mancini’s Italy – who beat France 3-1 three days ago – finish third but are safe from relegation.

items.title: World Bank ‘satisfied’ with $370m National Health Support Programme
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The World Bank has rated the implementation progress of its $370 million National Health Support Programme (NHSP) in Punjab, Sindh and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa as “satisfactory”, with a “moderate” overall risk rating, and expects the programme to meet its targets before the Dec 31, 2027 deadline. Effective since October 2022, the NHSP aims to advance universal health coverage by strengthening equitable access to and the quality of essential healthcare services at the primary level. The World Bank provided approximately $259m in financing, while the remaining funds came through grants and co-financing from the Global Financing Facility, the Gates Foundation, the Global Fund and Gavi. In its public disclosure, the Washington-based multilateral lender rated both, progress towards achieving the programme’s development objectives and overall implementation progress, as “satisfactory” while describing the overall risk as “moderate”. The NHSP “has sustained strong implementation momentum and continues to deliver tangible results across provinces”, the World Bank said, adding that approximately 76 per cent of total programme funding had been disbursed. Govt claims goods exports reached ‘all-time high’ of $11.4bn in July-October “Provincial governments have shown strong ownership, and the reforms introduced through the Disbursement Linked Results (DLRs) are strengthening primary health care systems. The remaining DLRs are on track, and all are expected to be achieved well ahead of the programme’s closing on Dec 31, 2027,” the bank noted. The World Bank has already disbursed $205m (79.3pc) of its $259m financing, while a $36.8m co-financing facility has been completely disbursed. Two other financing components of $35m and $29m have each recorded disbursements of 50pc, according to the lender. The programme uses a Program-for-Results (PforR) financing instrument, the first of its kind in Pakistan’s health sector, under which funding is linked to the achievement of agreed results. The approach builds on Pakistan’s universal health coverage reforms and improvements in implementation capacity demonstrated through the earlier National Immunisation Support Project, which included the federal health ministry and provincial governments. According to the World Bank, the programme’s improved health facility readiness score has reached 75pc in KP, 80pc in Punjab and 77.5pc in Sindh. However, the use of modern contraceptives among women of reproductive age remains relatively low at 15pc in KP, 30pc in Punjab and 20pc in Sindh. The NHSP complements existing investments in human capital and builds on reforms aimed at improving the quality of and equitable access to healthcare services. It focuses on three areas, including coverage and quality of essential healthcare services, governance and accountability and healthcare financing. Under the first component, the programme seeks to improve the availability of healthcare staff, supplies and essential medicines, while strengthening patient referral systems for emergency and higher-level care. Goods exports hit $11.4bn Separately, the federal government said the country’s goods exports had reached “an all-time high” of $11.4bn during July-October of the current fiscal year, registering year-on-year growth of 8.8pc from $10.4bn in the corresponding period last year, the state-run Associated Press of Pakistan reported. In a statement, the government attributed the performance to measures introduced in the federal budget and coordinated efforts by the finance team and relevant institutions. Published in Dawn, November 16th, 2026

items.title: Smog diplomacy
items.description: EACH winter, Lahore and Delhi engage in a peculiar rivalry, trading places at the top of the world’s air-pollution rankings . On Friday, Delhi was declared the world’s most polluted major city while Lahore slipped to seventh. For people breathing this air, the distinction offers little comfort. A change in the weather can improve a city’s ranking without removing the sources of pollution. The smog that settles over northern India and Pakistan comes from vehicle exhaust, industrial emissions, dust and agricultural fires, compounded by winter conditions that trap pollutants near the ground. Much of this pollution is generated locally, and both governments have work to do at home. In Pakistan’s Punjab, satellites detected 18,825 fires, most believed to involve crop-residue burning. Lahore exceeded national standards for fine particulate matter on all 40 days covered by a recent assessment. Punjab’s authorities report more inspections, penalties and closures targeting polluting industries and brick kilns. Enforcement is necessary, but its effects must outlast the smog season. There is also a regional dimension that neither government can afford to ignore. Polluted air crosses the border regardless of the state of bilateral relations. That makes the forthcoming visit of Pakistan’s climate change minister to New Delhi especially pertinent. He is due to attend an SCO gathering on civilisational dialogue. Air pollution is not the meeting’s purpose, but the visit offers a rare opportunity to broach practical cooperation with Indian officials. At a minimum, the two states could work towards jointly sharing air-quality measurements, forecasts, timely public health warnings and satellite information on crop fires. Their scientists could jointly examine how pollution travels across the border. Such efforts need not await a broader diplomatic thaw. Nor should they provide either side with an excuse to blame its neighbour for pollution it has failed to control at home. The SCO already provides a channel through which officials from both countries meet, despite strained relations. The minister should use that opening to make the case for sustained regular technical contact on smog. With millions enduring another winter of dangerous air, even a modest conversation would be useful. Published in Dawn, November 16th, 2026

items.title: Tenerife return to action after death of De Miguel
items.description: Tenerife played their first game since the death of striker Jesus de Miguel on an emotional day at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium. De Miguel died at the age of 30 on 3 November, a day after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a home match in Spain’s Segunda Division. Tenerife beat bottom side Ceuta 2-0 on Sunday, with tributes to De Miguel paid both before and during the game. Lengthy standing ovations preceded and followed a minute of silence before the match. In the ninth minute play was stopped and a round of applause took place, while a video of De Miguel was shown in the stadium, as happened at all first- and second-tier games in Spain last weekend. Tenerife fans displayed a banner that read: “Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally blue and white.” Forward Nacho Gil opened the scoring for the home side in the 40th minute and celebrated by holding up De Miguel’s shirt. Tenerife’s Enric Gallego carried a wreath of flowers on to the pitch Gil revealed a message written under his shirt that read: “Demi, always in our hearts.” Neal Viereck scored four minutes from time as Tenerife ended a run of six games without a win. They are 14th in the table. Tenerife’s game with Granada on 7 November was postponed and the club invited fans to the stadium to pay their respects to De Miguel. Owono was given a 12-match suspension by the Spanish football federation for the challenge which resulted in De Miguel’s death. The federation has ruled that the game between Tenerife and Andorra, which was abandoned seven minutes into stoppage time after the incident occurred, will not be replayed and the 2-2 score will stand.

items.title: United States thrash Haiti in Pochettino’s penultimate match
items.description: Mauricio Pochettino guided the United States to a thumping 6-0 win over Haiti in his penultimate game in charge. The former Tottenham manager only signed a new four-year deal with the USA in the summer but has agreed a two-and-a-half-year contract to replace Michael Carrick at Old Trafford. He will return to the Premier League next week after Tuesday’s Nations League quarter-final second leg with Haiti. And five second-half goals in Miami, including two from AC Milan winger Christian Pulisic, have made that match a formality. Pochettino praised his players for not allowing his impending departure to become a distraction. “I think we have an amazing future, brilliant future in this country with the national team,” Pochettino said. “I think if we want to go for big things, the structure and principles are here now and it’s only continuing. “The players were very, very professional from day one when they started to see all the rumours and then when we confirmed it a few days ago. “If you say to me, what we feel proud of, we feel so proud of the players and how they managed the situation in a mature way. “In the last two years, the kids, the young kids that appear, you can see how they play very relaxed because of what the experienced players provide, that platform to perform.” Folarin Balogun, the Monaco striker who almost joined Everton on transfer deadline day and who has been linked with a move to United himself, came off the bench to score the sixth goal of the night. He added: “The manager is an amazing guy, an amazing coach. “It’s always disappointing when a top coach leaves. But it’s part of the game, it’s part of the business. “I wish him the best in United. We have to build on the foundation he set. You’ve seen the intensity, the togetherness since he’s been in charge, and as his players we have a job to carry that on.” United paid a release clause in the region of £7.4m to extract Pochettino from his USA contract, with a further payment being made for his backroom staff. His first match in charge will be an away match against Liverpool on 22 November.

items.title: L’AS FAR qualifiée pour la Coupe des Champions Féminine de la FIFA 2027
items.description: Les joueuses de l’AS FAR ont confirmé leur suprématie sur le football africain en remportant, ce dimanche, la Ligue des champions féminine de la CAF. Les Marocaines ont dominé les Sud-Africaines de Mamelodi Sundowns (3-1) en finale, disputée au Suez Canal Stadium d’Ismaïlia, en Égypte, avec notamment un doublé d’Imane Touriss. Grâce à ce troisième sacre continental, un record dans la compétition, les protégées de Hicham El Idrissi ont validé leur qualification pour le deuxième tour de la Coupe des Champions Féminine de la FIFA 2027. Elles y affronteront les Nord-Coréennes de Naegohyang en décembre prochain. En cas de victoire, l’AS FAR décrochera son billet pour la phase finale, prévue en janvier 2027 à Miami. Les Militaires retrouveront ainsi une compétition qu’elles connaissent bien. Lors de la première édition, en 2026 à Londres, Fatima Tagnaout et ses coéquipières avaient atteint le stade des demi-finales. Ce nouveau sacre africain ouvre également à l’AS FAR les portes de la première Coupe du Monde des Clubs Féminine de la FIFA, programmée en janvier 2028. Par ailleurs, ce deuxième titre continental consécutif permet au TP Mazembe, champion d’Afrique en 2024, de décrocher également sa qualification pour ce rendez-vous mondial. items.title: We demand impeccable voter register
items.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, must urgently clean up its battered image by producing an impeccable voters’ register ahead of the 2027 general elections. The discovery that its own officials allegedly compromised the database through fraudulent registrations is a monumental embarrassment. It reinforces existing suspicions about the commission’s impartiality and competence at a time Nigerians desperately need an electoral umpire they can trust. The scale of the problem is alarming. Of the more than 11 million people registered during the 2026 Continuous Voter Registration, CVR, exercise, INEC’s Automated Biometric Identification System, ABIS, flagged approximately 1.5 million entries as suspicious. The commission subsequently removed 1,277,252 invalid records, leaving about 268,000 requiring further verification. The preliminary national register contains over 103.4 million voters. More disturbing is the alleged complicity of registration officers who abused their official login credentials to introduce fictitious identities. They reportedly uploaded AI-generated photographs, reused identical images and exploited registration provisions for persons with disabilities, claiming fictitious applicants had no fingers and could therefore bypass normal fingerprint verification. ABIS detected suspicious facial and biometric inconsistencies during screening. Artificial intelligence has consequently introduced a dangerous dimension toa electoral fraud. Its capacity to generate convincing human faces makes fabricating identities easier and visual inspection less reliable. Although digitally enhanced photographs of genuine applicants are not necessarily fraudulent, fictitious identities must be identified and eliminated. INEC says it has withdrawn implicated officers’ access credentials, commenced investigations, subjected suspicious entries to human adjudication and referred evidence for possible disciplinary action and prosecution. It promises further verification before the final register is displayed on December 15, 2026. These assurances are insufficient without demonstrable accountability. Public confidence in INEC was already fragile before this scandal. Controversies surrounding previous elections, particularly the disputed 2023 presidential election and the failure of IReV to upload results as expected, have deepened distrust. A manipulated register could facilitate fictitious voting identities, impersonation, inflated constituency figures and deliberate disenfranchisement of legitimate voters. Biometric accreditation may prevent some abuses, but cannot excuse a defective database. Professor JoashAmupitan must therefore open the corrective process to independent scrutiny. INEC should partner with opposition parties, civil society organisations, professional technology experts, the media and credible international electoral partners in conducting an independent forensic audit. The commission should publish state-by-state findings, preserve electronic evidence, identify and prosecute culprits, provide accessible mechanisms for genuine voters to challenge wrongful deletions and demonstrate BVAS and IReV readiness through independently observed tests. The December 15 deadline must be respected without sacrificing accuracy. Less than two months before the elections, Nigeria cannot afford administrative confusion that could undermine the transition to a new government. These elections belong to Nigerians, not incumbent governments or political parties. We demand an impeccable register, credible elections and leadership genuinely mandated by the Nigerian people. The post We demand impeccable voter register appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Portugal humbled in first game since Ronaldo retirement
items.description: Portugal suffered a heavy loss in their first game since Cristiano Ronaldo announced his international retirement as former Manchester United striker Rasmus Hojlund scored twice to help Denmark gain a superb victory. Ronaldo, 41, netted 146 goals and played 234 times for his country – both world records – since making his debut in 2003 and won the Ballon d’Or as the world’s best player on five occasions. But he retired from international football in a video posted on social media last week, even though coach Jorge Jesus later said Ronaldo would have been picked for the Uefa Nations League games against Denmark and Wales. The iconic forward walked out of the Portugal camp in September after being told he would not start the first match against Denmark, resulting in a £215 fine and 30-day suspension. Saturday’s game took place in Braga with the Portuguese fans and players paying tribute to Ronaldo. Each of the players and the mascots walked out wearing a ‘Ronaldo 7’ shirt, with the fans displaying the word ‘Ronaldo’ in the top tier of one of the stands and the letters ‘GOAT’ (Greatest Of All Time) on the bottom tier. The Portugal fans produced a tifo that said ‘Ronaldo goat’ as well as displaying a banner that translated as ‘thank you, captain’ There was also a banner that translated as ‘thank you, captain’, with a similar message appearing on the scoreboard in the seventh minute. But the party mood fell flat as Denmark cruised to a convincing win. Former Southampton and Tottenham midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg converted a penalty just before half-time to put the visitors ahead following a handball decision against Ruben Dias. Hojlund, who now plays in Italy with Napoli, then scored twice in an eight-minute spell early in the second half, before Fulham defender Joachim Andersen headed in the fourth to put the visitors 4-0 ahead after 75 minutes. Former Manchester City midfielder Bernardo Silva, now at Real Madrid, netted a consolation for Portugal in the third minute of added time with a close-range finish after Joao Neves had been denied. Portugal had won their opening four Nations League matches to secure their place in the quarter-finals and need to avoid defeat against Wales in Cardiff on Tuesday, 17 November, to progress as group winners. Denmark host Norway on Tuesday with a three-point advantage in second place. Ronaldo’s number seven shirt was handed to former Wolves forward Carlos Forbs, who now plays in Belgium for Club Brugge. However, the font had been changed to add a horizontal line through the ‘7’. A message from the official Portugal national team account on X said: “Time to debut a new 7. Because there’s one that will be eternal.”

items.title: Ben White has ‘exciting future’ despite boos – Declan Rice
items.description: Declan Rice has defended Arsenal teammate Ben White after the defender was booed at Wembley during England’s 2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday. White, who came on as a substitute in the Nations League fixture, left the Three Lions’ camp at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar to return home for personal reasons. He then made himself unavailable for selection for the rest of Gareth Southgate’s reign. White was also booed by some fans in March’s 1-1 draw with Ukraine after returning to the squad under Thomas Tuchel. “The incident with Ben was over five years ago, I don’t know why it is still a conversation to be honest,” Rice told BBC Radio 5 Live. “Knowing Ben, knowing the character he is, he has totally moved on from all of that. “He always wears the shirt with pride and every time he puts on the shirt, he gives 100 percent. “It shows his character. It is not easy being booed coming on at Wembley, but to show his mental strength to play the game and to play well, like he did in the previous months, is a real testament to him.” Rice also said that the players do not discuss the situation at all and that everybody has moved on, adding that White has “an exciting future ahead with this England squad”. Before the game, White said that people did not know the “full story” behind his departure from Qatar but that he still backed his decision. Rice close to signing new Arsenal contract By Sami Mokbel , Senior football correspondent Rice has also confirmed that he is close to signing a new contract with Arsenal . BBC Sport first revealed the midfielder was set to sign a new long-term deal at Emirates Stadium on 7 October, and the 27-year-old, speaking before England’s game against Spain on Sunday, said: “A new contract is hopefully on the horizon soon and I’m extremely lucky to be at a club like Arsenal where the manager shows me so much trust and teammates who put so much energy in to me.” Rice’s current deal expires in 2028, but the former West Ham star is now expected to extend his tenure in north London, having arrived from London Stadium in 2023 in a deal worth £105m. The midfielder’s new contract will put him alongside Bukayo Saka as Arsenal ‘s top earner. Rice has avoided upheaval throughout his career, and he believes continuity has helped him blossom. “I’ve been extremely lucky I’ve managed to play at such a consistent level throughout my career. I always set myself targets, pushing for more,” he said. “I’m extremely Lucky not to have to worry about that stuff, as it makes playing football far easier.”

items.title: Punjab working on first AI-run climate observatory
items.description: LAHORE: The Punjab Climate Observatory will be a milestone in the province’s efforts to address climate change, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif said on Sunday. Describing the under-construction facility as the first project of its kind in Pakistan, she wrote on social media platform X that the centre would conduct real-time monitoring of air quality, water, soil and weather conditions, supported by an artificial intelligence-powered climate intelligence system. The project was appr­oved in May 2025 following a review of its feasibility plan, covering budgetary requirements, equipment procurement and land acquisition. The Univer­sity of Engineering and Technology, Lahore, had also submitted a report on its technical aspects. In June, the chief minister directed the authorities to expedite work on the facility. In her statement, CM Maryam said the observatory would strengthen wea­­ther forecasting, early war­ning systems and flood prediction, helping impr­ove the province’s prepa­red­ne­ss for climate-related disasters. The facility would also house environmental data resources and research laboratories, providing young climate scientists with opportunities for learning and research, she added. The chief minister hoped the project would bring international scientific cooperation and research partnerships under one roof, while supporting evidence-based policymaking and public awareness. She said the observatory would contribute to disaster resilience, water conservation, sustainable resource management, climate-resilient agriculture and forest protection. “Our ambition is to empower the next generation of climate scientists and position Punjab as a regional leader and international partner in climate innovation, protecting our environment, communities and future generations,” she said. Published in Dawn, November 16th, 2026

items.title: Water demand outstrips supply in Punjab: UN agency
items.description: • FAO report says province losing 5.5bn cubic metres of groundwater annually • Highlights growing need for water resource management • Recommends setting up commission to review policies, existing strategies • Identifies shortcomings in data collection, info consolidation ISLAMABAD: A detailed assessment of Punjab’s water resources by a United Nations specialised agency has warned of serious challenges ahead, saying the province’s water demand already exceeds supply across all sectors. The Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said groundwater was being depleted by about 5.5 billion cubic metres annually over a five-year period, while surface water resources were also under growing pressure. To assess the province’s water stress, the FAO sought expert advice from water specialists, including former Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda) chairman Shamsul Mulk and former Indus River System Authority (Irsa) chairman Rao Irshad Ali Khan. The findings, published in a report titled Water and Land Accounting in Punjab, were based on annual water accounts covering five water years from 2012 to 2017. The report highlighted the growing need for comprehensive water resources management, saying Punjab required more advanced and integrated water services across different sectors and regions. It strongly recommended the establishment of a commission to conduct a one-time review of provincial water resources, water-related policies, institutional mandates and existing strategies. The commission’s tasks would include ensuring coherence between national and inter-provincial policies and water initiatives, and establishing an integrated mechanism to assess the impact of transboundary water projects and other interventions. It would also identify overlapping responsibilities and changes needed in institutional mandates, assess water and land resources, current demand and projections until 2050, and establish a provincial coordination cell within the Planning and Development Department for day-to-day operations. Given Punjab’s major contribution to the national economy, the management of its water resources is particularly critical, especially as Pakistan’s overall water supply is considered insecure. The gap between water supply and demand has become particularly acute in Punjab’s urban areas because of limited access to freshwater and declining groundwater reserves, the report observed. Agricultural production is also increasingly at risk because of water stress and the depletion of groundwater storage, it said. Freshwater shortages have led to greater reliance on the recycling of low-quality water, while pollution from agro-chemicals and urban wastewater has intensified. The analysis estimated that Punjab needed an additional 10 billion cubic metres of usable water annually to bridge the supply-demand gap and sustain its groundwater aquifer. It stressed the need for timely intervention, including exploring ways to increase surface water resources, improve gro­undwater recharge and develop provincial mechanisms for inter-seasonal water transfers. The report said rivers flowing through Punjab and its freshwater bodies had diminished significantly, with river flows declining by about 30 billion cubic metres following the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty with India. The province has only 1.7 per cent of wetland areas, while its natural landscape has declined considerably. Rainfall remains the only source of water outside canal command areas and urban centres, it noted. The report also observed that groundwater recharge sources had diminished, reducing the province’s net renewable water resources. Punjab’s canal system operates as a run-of-the-river system for half the year and cannot draw its full authorised share of river water. “The reduction in drainage flows suggests a consistent water supply and demand gap,” it added. A technical diagnosis of the water accounts identified four main challenges: increasing spatio-temporal water scarcity; continuous groundwater depletion; competition among sectors for water and unaccounted inter-sectoral water transfers; and the need to protect annual renewable water resources, wetlands and the natural landscape. The report also identified shortcomings in data collection and information consolidation. It recommended expanding the land-use classification system to cover the entire province. Published in Dawn, November 16th, 2026

items.title: ASUU Heroes Day, 2027 elections and the futuristic State Police, by Owei Lakemfa
items.description: It was one of the largest gatherings of Africa’s best brains. The date was November 12, the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) 2026 Heroes Day. The academics came from all parts of the country, gathering at the University of Abuja. Amongst them were current and former vice-chancellors, current and past presidents of ASUU, and founding NLC President, Comrade Hassan Sunmonu. There was Alhaji Mahmud Yayale Ahmed, who has held three of the country’s highest public offices: Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Head of the Civil Service, and Minister of Defence. Former Bauchi State Governor AhmaduAdamuMu’azu, ex-Permanent Secretaries Professor GokeAdegoroye and Dr. TimiebiKoripamo-Agary, who, as serving Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Labour and Productivity, sued a Minister for conduct bordering on corruption. Minister of State SuwaibaSa’idu Ahmad, a professor of Science Education, held herself up as a proud member of ASUU, identified the principle of good welfare for academics, and urged all to continuously help build bridges between Government and ASUU. The occasion embodied three primary characteristics of the seventy-eight-year-old ASUU. First, ever analysing the past, which is why it annually marks its Heroes Day to honour those who have made sacrifices for the union, universities, and the country. The Day commemorates November 12, 2013, the date former ASUU President and noted novelist Festus Iyayi was killed in a car crash. He was travelling for an ASUU National Executive Council meeting in Kano to find a solution to a national strike triggered by Government’s intransigence and insistence on defunding education. The second ASUU culture is ever interrogating the present, which is why this year’s theme focused on the electoral system. The third is the union’s tendency to probe into the future. This time, it looked at the ongoing attempts to create State Police and the possible impact it could have on the 2027 General Elections. ASUU is also quite strategic in building alliances, which is why its awardees this year included a number of people who led the Government Negotiating Teams or played roles in ensuring the success of the decades-long ASUU-Government negotiations. These included Alhaji Ahmed, Professor MunzaliJibril, whose Negotiating Team in May 2021 broke through barriers and successfully produced a draft agreement, and Professor NimiDimkpa Briggs, who, on June 16, 2022, despite government reservations, followed through with a new draft agreement within ten weeks. The Buhari government had been so displeased with the breakthrough the Briggs Team had made with ASUU that it made false accusations against the likeable professor. It accused him of excluding government agencies from the negotiations, inflating academics’ salaries by N1.1 trillion, and acting out of financial self-interest. In making the last two allegations, it escaped the government’s mind that Briggs had retired from service and, as such, would not be a beneficiary of the enhanced academics’ pay. When Briggs passed on ten months later, the same Buhari government praised him to high heavens for his dignity, truthfulness, and “historic contributions” to education. Alhaji Ahmed, speaking on behalf of the awardees, joked about his experience with ASUU President Chris Piwuna, a professor of psychiatry whom he said tried to make him his patient, but he rejected such negotiation tactics. He dedicated his award to former ASUU President and current Trustee, Professor AsisiAsobie, whom he said introduced him to the union’s unique ways of negotiation. Asobie, he said, would refuse to even drink water in his office because they were negotiating. Professor Piwuna, in analysing the situation in the country, said: “The Nigerian Universities and our members have suffered their share of violence and trauma. Some campuses were attacked; we have lost members across branches, and several students have been killed, staff displaced, and properties lost. Our universities have become theatres of ‘war’ and easy targets for insurgents, from Jos to Abuja, and campuses in North West Nigeria.” I had the honour of delivering the 2026 ASUU Annual Lecture titled: ‘Insecurity, Incumbency and Elections in Nigeria: The Role of State Police.’ I pointed out that in the past eleven years of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) administrations of Buhari and Tinubu, at least 97,111 persons have been killed in violent conflicts. Also, that Nigeria, in the 2026 Global Terrorism Index (GTI) Report, ranks fourth globally, trailing Pakistan, Burkina Faso, and Niger. I therefore submitted that even with the assistance of the military, the police are not coping with insecurity. I listed challenges of the police as including their inability to wean themselves of their colonial origins of relying on force, repression, and suppression of Nigerians rather than being a civil agency and a friend of the people. Other problems I mentioned are very poor remuneration and welfare and job insecurity, particularly amongst its top echelons. One of the suggestions I made was that, career-wise, the police should be run like the public service, where the promotion of a few as Permanent Secretaries or Head of Service does not mean all the Directors senior to them are sacked. In the alternative, that a non-policeman, such as a judge or senior lawyer, be made the Inspector General of Police (IGP). If a non-soldier can be the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, a non-policeman can be the IGP. These challenges, I posited, make the establishment of State Police necessary, especially when they will be recruited from locals familiar with the terrain and local culture. The fact that there will be multiple police agencies would not lead to administrative challenges, as the United States runs 17,985 police agencies and Canada, 160. The challenges I see include whether state governments that cannot pay workers’ salaries can afford State Police or whether governors who employ thugs would not recruit them into the State Police. Again, can state governors that would not allow their State Electoral Commissions or Local Governments to run properly allow professionalism in their State Police? Our politics itself, I submitted, is being transformed into a criminal enterprise in which true primaries are hardly held, opposition supporters are beaten and prevented from casting their ballots or threatened with death, and results are written sometimes before elections. I submitted that elections in the country, which should be as simple as the holder of the National Identity Card voting at any polling unit and their vote being automatically transmitted to central and local collation centres, have been made unnecessarily cumbersome with voter cards, ballot papers, card readers, BVAS, IREV, collation centres, etcetera. My conclusion is that, with the Presidential Elections nine weeks away, it is unlikely the State Police will be in place before then. Even if it is, with 32 governors siding with the ruling party and an unreformed police, no fundamental changes to the usual partisan policing will take place The post ASUU Heroes Day, 2027 elections and the futuristic State Police, by Owei Lakemfa appeared first on Vanguard News .
